Now, when Duke was coming up, when he started, Irving Mills was his mentor, I guess you'd say, and every bar of music Duke Ellington wrote, Irving Mills' name was on it. Irving -- and Duke Ellington used to write all this music and he used to write a tremendous amount of blues and things, you know, or bluesy type things, which contributed to his reputation. I mean moreso than just playing the average popular songs. So Duke got that idea. So I think consciously or subsonsciously or whatever, he was getting back at…
I see. He was making up for his lost --
